title: Set an exam table's stirrups: draw each out, unfold it, lift it out of its lock and drop it into the outermost notch
instruction: Set this exam table's stirrups for an exam: both out, unfolded and locked in their outermost positions.
context: Setting stirrups is part of a medical assistant's listed task (O*NET 31-9092, 833,900 employed): "Prepare treatment rooms for patient examinations"; about 44 million US pelvic exams were done in 2012 (Am Fam Physician). Table: Midmark Ritter 204 class (27 in top). Its guide: "A) Pull the stirrup out, then unfold. B) Lift the stirrup slightly, then move it left or right as desired. C) Release stirrup to lock in position." Caution: "Be sure the stirrups are locked in place before using." The wrong state that looks right: a stirrup swung out and let go between positions rests unlocked on the bracket's teeth. The parts hold the order: a folded stirrup cannot turn up inside the shelf; a bar swings only with its end lifted. Unlike a mitre saw's turntable swung to its 45 degree detent (TK-K64735) or a suitcase handle drawn out to its lock (TK-28LP2A), each stirrup chains five gated motions (draw, unfold, lift out of its detent, shift, drop into a notch), one arm per side.
setup: Two YAM arms (pads open 94 mm), bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the bench. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x out, y left; heights above the bench. The foot end of a manual exam table (Midmark Ritter 204 class), its upperwrap and footrest shelf with the upholstered top, clamped to the bench: powder-coated 1.5 mm sheet steel, 67 cm wide, 58 cm deep, 22 cm tall, with a 6 cm vinyl cushion, its front face at x 65, centred on y 0; its rear 32 cm overhangs the bench's far edge onto a welded steel support stand (32 x 60 cm top plate at bench height, four 4 cm square legs). Footrest pushed in. Two stirrup assemblies, bars at y +-24.5, 14 cm up: each a 3/4 x 1/4 in steel bar 56.5 cm long (0.53 kg) through a pivot boss 5 cm behind the face, drawing out 40 cm to a collar; a chrome stirrup (0.30 kg, 25 cm from its roll pin to the tip of a 7 cm wide teardrop loop) on a roll pin at the bar's front end, folded flat along the bar; a 6 mm detent post 30 mm tall on the bar's tail, pressed up by the guide bracket's leaf spring (about 11 N) into an 8 mm wide, 5 mm deep groove along the draw and notches at 12 deg inward, straight, 12 and 24 deg outward. Start: both stowed (bar in, stirrup folded, only its 38 mm hinge end showing through a 9 x 3.4 cm window in the face). Both arms at their ready poses, grippers open.
scoring: Checked with a ruler, a protractor on the boss and the trial video once everything is still. Each stirrup counts only once both grippers have been at least 3 cm from it (its bar and stirrup) and no point of it has moved more than 1 mm, both for the last 1 s. It earns 2 points if it is fully out (within 8 mm of its collar), unfolded (within 5 deg of its open stop) and locked in its outermost position (swung within 2 deg of 24 deg outward and let down: the bar within 1.5 deg of level, the post up in the notch), 1 point if out and unfolded but not locked there, 0 otherwise. Score: points / 4 (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0). 0 for good if a stirrup is ever forced 3 deg or 3 mm past one of its stops.
reset_notes: For each stirrup: lift its end slightly, swing it straight until the post drops into the groove's end, fold the stirrup flat along its bar, and push the bar into the shelf until only the stirrup's hinge end (38 mm) shows. Arms to their ready poses.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the sizes in the README's parts table, all estimated (none published); shelf fixed. Free joints with real stops and light damping: the boss's swing, the bar's lift and draw, the stirrup's roll pin. The order is held by contact: the window over the folded stirrup, the bracket's groove and notches. The detent post is our modelling choice for how the bar's tail engages the guide bracket, which the maker does not draw. The leaf spring is a 12 N m/rad spring at the bar's lift.
